docs.title: Galaxy Zoo 2 Dataset
docs.text:
The Galaxy Zoo 2 project by (Willett et al., 2013), which contains morphological classifications of galaxies based on volunteer votes. The votes are decided using tree based questiosn, where each question has morphogological features as answers.

The desiciion tree has 11 main questions with 37 possible answers. Each answer is represented as a column in the dataset, and the value in each column represents the fraction of volunteers who voted for that answer for a given galaxy. The desicion tree is shown below:

Figure 1: Galaxy Zoo 2 decision tree Willett et al., 2013

About 16 million classifications were made by volunteers for 304,122 galaxies, resulting in a rich dataset for morphological analysis.

The dataset contains a total of 304,122 samples, each corresponding to a unique galaxy. The dataset is available in CSV format and can be accessed through the Galaxy Zoo 2 data release. Ultimately voting fractions for each answer are used as labels for training machine learning models to classify galaxy morphologies.

docs.title: Label Processing
docs.text: In this section, I will discuss different methods of label processing on Galaxy Zoo 2 dataset used in this project. The dataset contains 11 columns of labels, each representing a different morphological feature of galaxies. The labels are in the form of probabilities, indicating the likelihood of a galaxy having a particular feature.

docs.title: T07 Argmax Rule (Classes 0–2)
docs.text:
Among \(f_{\text{completely round}}\), \(f_{\text{in-between}}\), and \(f_{\text{cigar-shaped}}\), assign the class with the highest vote fraction, provided:

\[\max(f_{\text{completely round}},\ f_{\text{in-between}},\ f_{\text{cigar-shaped}}) \geq 0.50\]

If the maximum falls below \(0.50\), the sample is dropped as ambiguous.

docs.title: Exclusivity Guard Logic
docs.text:
The top-level branch is determined by a strict if/elif on T01:

\[ \text{Branch} = \begin{cases} \text{Smooth (Classes 0--2)} & \text{if } f_{\text{smooth}} \geq 0.469 \text{ and } f_{\text{features/disk}} < 0.430 \\ \text{Disk (Classes 3--4)} & \text{if } f_{\text{features/disk}} \geq 0.430 \text{ and } f_{\text{smooth}} < 0.469 \\ \text{Drop (ambiguous)} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Class distribution for Method 1 without sampling

The class distribution is highly imbalanced, with Class 4 (Spiral) being the most populous and Class 2 (Cigar-shaped smooth) being the least populous. This imbalance may affect model training and evaluation, necessitating techniques such as class weighting or resampling to mitigate bias towards the majority class.

docs.title: Balancing Using Class Weights
docs.text:
Class balacing using pytorch's WeightedRandomSampler. The weights are computed as the inverse of the class frequencies, giving more importance to minority classes during training.

Figure 2: Class weights for Method 1 for 1k samples

To address the class imbalance, we can compute class weights inversely proportional to the class frequencies. This allows the model to give more importance to minority classes during training, potentially improving performance on underrepresented classes.

docs.title: Model Overview
docs.text: This architecture is a custom deep residual convolutional neural network designed for 5-class galaxy image classification. The network follows a bottleneck-style ResNet structure with residual skip connections, progressive spatial downsampling, batch normalization, dropout regularization, and global average pooling.

docs.title: Residual Learning
docs.text: The network employs residual shortcut connections to: - Improve gradient propagation - Reduce vanishing gradient problems - Enable deeper architectures

docs.title: Bottleneck Design
docs.text:
Each residual unit follows: 1. 1×1 reduction convolution 2. 3×3 feature extraction convolution 3. 1×1 expansion convolution

This reduces computational complexity while preserving representational power.

docs.title: Downsampling Strategy
docs.text: Spatial resolution reduction occurs progressively: - 64×64 → 32×32 → 16×16 → 8×8 → 4×4

docs.title: Regularization
docs.text: Dropout layers are inserted within bottleneck units and before the classifier head to reduce overfitting.

docs.title: Final Output
docs.text: The model produces: - A 5-dimensional probability vector - Corresponding galaxy class prediction via softmax activation
